```{python}
import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

ksel = pd.read_csv("outputs/k_selection.csv")
clusters = pd.read_parquet("outputs/clusters.parquet")
summary = json.load(open("outputs/summary.json"))
k = summary["k"]
```

k-means on nine z-scored features (utility-supplied, prestadores IRCA; piped water and
sewer coverage; poverty; rural share; altitude; rainfall; municipal performance; log SGP
water transfers per person), `{python} f"{len(clusters):,}"` zone-years, 2016–2023. The
analysis chose **k = `{python} k`**: `{python} summary["k_reason"]`

## Choosing k

::: {layout-ncol=2}

```{python}
#| label: fig-elbow
#| fig-cap: "Elbow plot: k-means inertia (within-cluster sum of squares) by k."
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of inertia falling as k rises from 2 to 8, with the chosen k marked."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5, 3.2))
ax.plot(ksel["k"], ksel["inertia"], marker="o")
ax.axvline(k, color="grey", linestyle="--")
ax.set_xlabel("k (number of clusters)")
ax.set_ylabel("Inertia")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-silhouette
#| fig-cap: "Mean silhouette (−1 to 1) by k, on a fixed sample of rows."
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of the mean silhouette by k from 2 to 8, around 0.17 to 0.24, with the chosen k marked."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5, 3.2))
ax.plot(ksel["k"], ksel["silhouette"], marker="o", color="#b5651d")
ax.axvline(k, color="grey", linestyle="--")
ax.set_xlabel("k (number of clusters)")
ax.set_ylabel("Mean silhouette")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

:::

## A picture of the clusters

```{python}
#| label: fig-pca
#| fig-cap: "Each dot is a zone-year on the first two principal components of the nine z-scored features, coloured by cluster. PCA is only for the picture; k-means used all nine features."
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of about eleven thousand zone-years in four coloured, overlapping groups on the first two principal components."
colors = ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3", "#e7298a", "#66a61e", "#e6ab02", "#a6761d", "#666666"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
for c, g in clusters.groupby("cluster"):
    ax.scatter(g["pc1"], g["pc2"], s=4, alpha=0.5, color=colors[c - 1], label=f"Cluster {c}")
ax.set_xlabel(f"PC1 ({summary['pca_variance_pc1']:.0%} of variance)")
ax.set_ylabel(f"PC2 ({summary['pca_variance_pc2']:.0%} of variance)")
ax.legend(markerscale=4, frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## What sets each cluster apart?

```{python}
profiles = pd.read_csv("outputs/cluster_profiles.csv").set_index("cluster")
names = profiles["name"].to_dict()
pcolors = profiles["color"].to_dict()
features = ["irca", "water_coverage", "sewer_coverage", "ipm", "rural_share", "altitude_m",
            "rainfall_mm", "mdm", "log_sgp_water_pc"]
labels = ["IRCA (prestadores)", "Piped water", "Sewer", "Poverty (IPM)", "Rural share",
          "Altitude", "Rainfall", "MDM", "log SGP water / person"]
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Cluster mean z-scores: standard deviations above (red) or below (blue) the year's average. IRCA is utility-supplied (prestadores)."
#| fig-alt: "Heatmap of four clusters by nine features, blue for below-average and red for above-average values, with each cell's mean z-score printed."
z = profiles[[f"z_{f}" for f in features]].to_numpy()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.4))
im = ax.imshow(z, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-1.5, vmax=1.5, aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(features)), labels, rotation=30, ha="right")
ax.set_yticks(range(len(profiles)), [f"{c} · {names[c]}" for c in profiles.index])
for i in range(z.shape[0]):
    for j in range(z.shape[1]):
        ax.text(j, i, f"{z[i, j]:+.1f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8)
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="z")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Outcomes by cluster and year

Outcomes describe the clusters; they were never used to form them. These differences are
descriptive and do not establish causal effects of water quality. Infant mortality is shown
for 2017–2019 and 2021–2023 only; Saber 11 only in published years.

```{python}
#| label: fig-outcomes
#| fig-cap: "Median outcome by cluster and year. Missing years are gaps, not joined lines."
#| fig-alt: "Three line charts by year, one per outcome (infant mortality, Saber 11 score, dropout), one line per cluster, with gaps in years without data."
outcomes = pd.read_csv("outputs/outcomes_by_year.csv")
titles = {"infant_mortality": "Infant mortality per 1,000 births",
          "saber11_mean": "Saber 11 mean score", "dropout_rate": "School dropout (%)"}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10, 3.4))
for ax, (col, title) in zip(axes, titles.items()):
    o = outcomes[outcomes["outcome"] == col]
    for c, g in o.groupby("cluster"):
        g = g.set_index("year").reindex(range(2016, 2024))   # missing years become gaps
        ax.plot(g.index, g["median"], marker="o", color=pcolors[c], label=names[c])
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10, loc="left")
    ax.set_xticks([2016, 2019, 2022])
fig.legend(*axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels(), loc="lower center", ncol=2, frameon=False,
           bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.12), fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Worse water, more infant deaths? Within-cluster check

```{python}
#| label: fig-within
#| fig-cap: "Median infant mortality (per 1,000 live births) by utility-supplied (prestadores) IRCA band, within each cluster; 2017–2019 and 2021–2023 pooled, one row per municipality-year. ρ is Spearman's rank correlation of IRCA with infant mortality; n counts municipality-years."
#| fig-alt: "Four small panels, one per cluster, showing median infant mortality across the IRCA bands from no risk to unfit, with Spearman's rho and n printed on each; the lines are nearly flat."
rho = pd.read_csv("outputs/irca_infant.csv").set_index("cluster")
bins = pd.read_csv("outputs/irca_infant_bins.csv")
band_order = ["No risk", "Low", "Medium", "High", "Unfit"]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(rho), figsize=(10, 3), sharey=True)
for ax, (c, g) in zip(axes, bins.groupby("cluster")):
    g = g.set_index("irca_band").reindex(band_order)
    ax.plot(range(5), g["median"], marker="o", color=pcolors[c])
    ax.set_xticks(range(5), ["N", "L", "M", "H", "U"])
    ax.set_title(f"Cluster {c}", fontsize=10, loc="left", color=pcolors[c])
    ax.text(0.04, 0.06, f"ρ = {rho.loc[c, 'spearman_rho']:+.2f}\nn = {rho.loc[c, 'n']:,}",
            transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=9)
axes[0].set_ylabel("Infant mortality per 1,000")
fig.supxlabel("IRCA band: N no risk · L low · M medium · H high · U unfit", fontsize=9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-rho
#| tbl-cap: "Spearman's ρ between utility-supplied (prestadores) IRCA and infant mortality, within each cluster."
from IPython.display import Markdown
t = rho[["spearman_rho", "n", "municipalities"]].copy()
t.insert(0, "kind", [names[c] for c in t.index])
t["spearman_rho"] = t["spearman_rho"].map("{:+.2f}".format)
Markdown(t.to_markdown())
```

This comparison is descriptive: it does not establish a causal effect of water quality on
infant mortality, because poverty, rurality, health-service access and reporting quality
differ between places, and infant mortality is measured for the whole municipality while
IRCA is measured per zone.
